clue.text: After meal recirculated Port Said plan

indicators.note: recirculated means sent round again in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan for Port Said, the Egyptian harbour city, is being passed round again.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived adjective describes something happening once a meal is finished, such as a nap or a stroll.

clue.text: Awful pass, note: footballer George over the hill?

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly done, so these letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer of the 1960s and 70s

explanation.surface: A sports commentator mocks a poor pass by an ageing George Best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges PASS and NOTE into PASTONES. George Best was a celebrated Manchester United winger whose career faded early.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being in decline after your peak years, the question mark flagging the phrase sense.

clue.text: Starts to sense trouble, objections, about the weasel-like mammal

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone senses trouble and raises objections about a weasel-like animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This brown mustelid, ermine in winter, is a close relative of the weasel.

clue.text: Become tiresome about computers following unexpected difficulty

indicators.note: about means the first piece wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to pall is to become tiresome or dull
IT, information technology, stands for computers
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Computers grow tiresome when you keep hitting snags.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden danger or trap; figuratively a hidden or unforeseen problem.

clue.text: Mother turns up with article for girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother
and means with, joining things together
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A mother arrives with some item for her daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a common girl's first name, so girl stands for it by example.

clue.text: Doctor brought over a paper — preliminary outline

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought over means the first piece is placed above the next

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A doctor fetches a newspaper and hands over a sketch plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A first version of a document or plan, to be revised later.

clue.text: After beginning of August change entire course

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the first letter
beginning of means the first letter of the following word is taken
change means the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: After early August, someone revises an entire course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns ENTIRE into INTREE. AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Course here means a racecourse, and this one is England's most famous jumps venue.

clue.text: Ways a teacher is far superior

parts.note: streets are roads or ways
a head is a head teacher, the senior teacher in a school

explanation.surface: A teacher walks the streets and proves herself better than all.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for being much better than rivals.

clue.text: Attempt to contain resistance is of limited duration

indicators.note: to contain means the first word's letters hold the other inside them

parts.note: a shot is an attempt or try
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: An effort to hold back opposition proves brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief in time; not lasting long.

clue.text: Opposed to introduction of agreed profits before time

indicators.note: before places profits ahead of time in the answer
introduction of means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: gains are profits

explanation.surface: Someone objects to bringing in agreed profits too soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning in opposition to, as in voting against a motion.

clue.text: Unacceptable charge for going away

parts.note: out means not acceptable, as in a suggestion being out
a ward is someone in another's charge, such as a minor under a guardian

explanation.surface: A fee for leaving is deemed unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a departing journey, as in the outbound leg of a trip.

clue.text: Recall some sledges, retorts, abrupt

indicators.note: Recall says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cricket memory of sharp on-field taunts and curt comebacks; sledging is verbal baiting of batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ESRET from the end of sledges and the start of retorts, and 'Recall' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe speech that is brief to the point of rudeness.

clue.text: English like the Italian boy ultimately without difficulty

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
il is Italian for the

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An English lad, like the Italian boy, manages things effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning with ease, simply and comfortably.

clue.text: Act of worship where sermon's half missed out — quite a failing!

indicators.note: half missed out means only the first half of the word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing or weakness

explanation.surface: A churchgoer complains that skipping half the sermon is quite a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half missed out' keeps SER, the front half of the sermon's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A church gathering for worship, such as evensong, is called by this name.

clue.text: Cheerful as pub refurbished, adding seats internally

indicators.note: adding places the next piece after the rearranged letters
refurbished means done up anew, so these letters are rearranged
internally means the inner letters of the word, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: Drinkers are happy that their local has been done up with new seating inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is only a link here; 'adding' puts the inside of seats after the reworked pub, and 'refurbished' and 'internally' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adjective for optimistic and positive in mood.

clue.text: Artist in biopic as son

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A painter appears in a film about his life, playing his own son.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo, the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, is the artist meant.

clue.text: Prohibition ended, almost? Exactly right!

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: gone means ended or finished

explanation.surface: Someone cheers that a ban has very nearly ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British exclamation of approval meaning spot on or precisely correct.

clue.text: On return steal one's man?

indicators.note: on return means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rob is to steal
one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether coming back to steal makes them the right man.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, given by example; the question mark signals the definition by example.

clue.text: Salesman's talk, special, that is lame principally

parts.note: ie, from Latin id est, means that is

indicators.note: principally means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A salesman's special pitch is, frankly, rather lame.
explanation.definitionFit: A glib, rehearsed patter used to persuade, typical of a sales pitch.

clue.text: Song about ungentlemanly guy in rural setting?

indicators.note: about means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A ballad tells of a bounder in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek region became a poetic byword for an idyllic pastoral paradise.

clue.text: Cherished hope of daughter in relation to time before midday

parts.note: re means concerning or in relation to
a.m. marks the hours before noon

explanation.surface: A parent's fond wish about their daughter concerns the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration or ambition one longs to fulfil.

clue.text: Quiet home doubly good greatly admired

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: doubly means the word is used twice over

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A quiet home that is doubly good wins great admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: As in a shining example: outstanding and held up as a model.

clue.text: Embarrassing display noticed, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard, so a word sounding alike is entered

parts.note: seen means noticed

explanation.surface: Reports say an awkward public outburst was spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a fuss in public, as in causing an embarrassing outburst.

clue.text: Being knowledgeable, remind fellow going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A clever person reminds a colleague who is making mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone who has a lot of information on a subject.
